question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ which of the following could be the second column of the matrix $P?$

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,z=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the Jordan matrix $J$ may be written as a composition of Jordan blocks, as follows:

$$
J={J}_{2}(-1)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(-1)
$$

So, we have

- one $2\times 2$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =-1,$ and

- one $1\times 1$ Jordan block corresponding to $\lambda =-1.$

Therefore, the columns of $P$ form the following chains: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{2}(-1) & : & {v}_{2}\overset{A+I\,}{\to }{v}_{1}\overset{A+I\,}{\to }0 &  \\ {J}_{1}(-1) & : & {v}_{3}\overset{A+I\,}{\to }0 & \end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the second column of $P$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2$ corresponding to $\lambda =-1.$ 

Now, computing $A+I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A+I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Among the given vectors, only $y$ is a generalized eigenvector of rank $2,$ since

$$
(A+I)y=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=x,
$$

and, therefore,

$$
(A+I)^{2}y=(A+I)x=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 0 \\ -4 & 2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],
$$

and we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\overset{A+I\,}{\to }[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\overset{A+I\,}{\to }0.\end{aligned}
$$

The other vectors do not satisfy this condition.
